_about: The Stargazer Pyramids and the Solport Dark Sky Observatory (plan_stargaze.js). Every name, line of copy, size, light level and position is here so it can be changed without touching code. World metres: x = east, z = south. rot is the yaw in degrees (180 = the deck and door face north). Rules: no em dashes, no prices, no percentages, no investment language. If you move the site, also move the three stamps of the 'darksky' chapter in plan/progress.json.

sign.k: A dark sky retreat · Stage Three · The Expanse
sign.p: Fourteen glass pyramids on raised timber decks in the desert of the Ridge Arroyo, each with panoramic triple pane glass, smart glass that switches from clear to frosted, a telescope by the glass, a king bed under the stars, and a private deck with a hot tub and a fire pit. The Solport Dark Sky Observatory sits at the heart of the retreat. Every light out here is shielded, amber and pointed down.

observatory.p: The dome opens its slit after sunset. Inside, a large reflecting telescope tracks tonight's targets under dim red light that keeps your night vision. Talks run at the Star Theatre beside the dome, and the Stargazing Terrace has loungers for anyone who wants to lie back and look up.

terrace.k: Lie back · E on any lounger
terrace.p: A ring of zero gravity loungers on a gravel terrace with almost no light of its own. Lie back, let your eyes adapt, and look up. The bronze compass rose in the centre shows north, where Polaris holds still while the sky turns around it.

theatre.p: Stone tiers around a fire pit lounge, open toward the dome. The resident astronomer gives short talks here after dark about what is up tonight.

model.k: Open for anyone to walk through
model.p: Walk in through the glass door: a king bed that faces up through the glass, a lounge with a sofa and a fireplace, a dining table, a full kitchen with an espresso machine, a spa bathroom with a rain shower and a telescope by the glass. Switch the smart glass from clear to frosted by the door.

bed: A king bed under the apex
The bed faces up through the glass so you fall asleep under the Milky Way. Press E to lie back and stargaze.
lounge: A deep sofa in front of a suspended fireplace, warm enough for a desert winter night.
kitchen: Full kitchen with an espresso machine
A stone counter, an induction cooktop, a small fridge drawer and an espresso machine for the morning after a late night.
bath: A rain shower, a stone vessel basin and a frosted glass screen that keeps the stars in view above it.
dining: Dinner for two under the apex
A walnut table for two with the whole sky as the ceiling.

astronomer.name: Dr. Celeste Ruiz
astronomer.role: Resident Astronomer · Solport Dark Sky Observatory
greet: Give your eyes twenty minutes. The sky keeps getting better.
Clear skies tonight. Come and look.
Red light only out here, it keeps your night vision.

talk.t: Welcome to the Solport Dark Sky Observatory. Out here, on a moonless night, the Milky Way is bright enough to cast a faint glow on the sand. What would you like to know?
o: Why is it so dark here?
Why is it so dark here?

talk.t: Southern Arizona is one of the best stargazing regions in the country: high desert, dry air and very few city lights. Every fixture at the retreat is shielded, amber and pointed down, so no light goes up into the sky. Give your eyes twenty to thirty minutes in the dark and you will see several times more stars. Red light does not undo that, which is why the dome glows red inside.

Lie back on any lounger on the terrace, or on the bed in the Model Pyramid, and press E. Drag to look around the sky. C draws the constellations, T puts you behind the telescope, L runs a short star trail time lapse, and the list of what is up tonight swings your view onto a target. E or Esc to get up again.

Fourteen glass pyramids, some about five hundred square feet and some about eight hundred, each on its own timber deck with a hot tub and a fire pit. The glass is triple pane, and the smart glass switches from clear to frosted when you want privacy. The Model Pyramid next to the theatre is open to everyone.

astronomer.tonightFallback: Tonight, look north for Polaris, which holds still while everything else wheels around it, and follow the Milky Way from horizon to horizon. Lie back on a lounger and give your eyes a few minutes.
kw: Lie back on a lounger and press E. The list of what is up tonight points you straight at it.
